name: Dmitri Osei-Vandenberghe
creator: Dmitri Osei-Vandenberghe
description: Osei-Vandenberghe builds monumental sculptures from discarded augmentation hardware — obsolete chrome limbs, dead BCI housings, rejected geneware applicators — welded into figures of overwhelming physical presence that he installs without permission in Tier 2 and Tier 3 public spaces overnight. Each sculpture is accompanied by a small plaque bearing only the name of the person whose discarded augmentation hardware was used, sourced from medical waste manifests he obtains through underground channels. His work treats the human body's discarded technological extensions as something worthy of monument.
medium: physical sculpture / salvage chrome / augmentation hardware
cultural_impact: The named-plaque practice transformed his sculptures from aesthetic objects into community monuments, and several have been adopted by the neighborhoods where they appeared, with residents fighting removal orders. His work is credited as a founding influence on the Ironbloom chrome pride movement.
controversy: The medical waste manifests he uses to identify hardware donors are obtained illegally; several of the named individuals have objected to being commemorated without consent, while others have traveled across GLMZ to find the sculptures bearing their names. HelixCorp's waste management division has filed ongoing injunctions.
story_hooks: One of Osei-Vandenberghe's named plaques commemorates hardware from someone who is officially listed as still living — and who has no record of any augmentation procedure.
A Tier 5 collector has begun purchasing his sculptures immediately after installation, before communities can claim them; Osei-Vandenberghe wants this stopped but the sales are technically legal.

He has gone silent and the sculptures have stopped appearing; a single unfinished piece was found in his studio, and the name on its plaque belongs to someone who disappeared from the Shelf three months ago.
